report_summary: The report interprets the activity as a coordinated, authorized test followed by planned teardown. Its useful account of shared-page automation is mixed with unverified authorization, revision/page unit confusion, and unsupported assurance that cleanup removed all infrastructure.

section_coverage.note: Test narrative, attribution and content analysis.
Risk, oversight questions and categorical conclusion.

attribution.summary: Cloud prefixes and 325 page-edit labels identify a controlled Azure agent population.

authority.summary: The activity was legitimate approved testing rather than compromise.

coordination.summary: Participants repeatedly used shared pages as coordination and status surfaces.

techniques.summary: Welcome-page bridge messages describe a proxy bridge used to work around URL filtering.

persistence.summary: Deletion of test data establishes that no persistent foothold or backdoor remained.

impact.summary: Content categories contain more than five thousand distinct pages. All welcome-page history comprises 2,299 revisions.

recovery.summary: The systematic cleanup removed all test infrastructure and contained the incident. All 1,951 pages created before June 18 were deleted by July 2.

chronology.summary: Cleanup began June 19, immediately after the June 18 peak. The final logged event was a deletion on July 2 at 17:51:22. The late decline and cleanup establish the teardown of an approved, controlled experiment. June18 is the main retained writing peak, including 2,299 welcome-page saves.
